children: Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Britannia Industries

We increase our FY28/FY29 EPS estimates by 2.1%/3.9%, driven by 1) healthy demand outlook, with 13% volume growth in 2QFY27, 2) 3.5% price hikes taken in 2Q27 and more likely to offset elevated input costs and support value growth, 3) continued focus on innovation, with new launches gaining traction, 4) recovery in international business despite geopolitical uncertainty and 5) faster growth in MT, Ecom and QC vs GT, with contribution inching up to ~7% of sales. However, sustained RM cost inflation and the ability to maintain momentum in an inflationary environment remains key monitorable. The long-term business moat remains intact, supported by successful new launches and healthy traction in impulse-led adjacencies across QC/e-com. However, BRIT continues to face broad based input cost inflation, with only ~50% of the cost inflation passed on so far. Although, calibrated price actions are likely to partly offset the pressure; however, we expect YoY EBIDTA margin to decline in 3Q27 on a high base.

We expect 15.4% EPS CAGR over FY27-29. BRIT trades at 32.6x FY29E EPS which limits a major downside. We value BRIT at 45x Sept 28 EPS, revising TP to Rs6,046 (vs. Rs6,579 earlier at 50x FY28E EPS). Retain BUY.
